function.description: Read part of one UTF-8 workspace text file. path must be a real file you have already seen in an ls, find, or search result; read never accepts a directory, a glob, or a filename you inferred from a language or framework convention. Returns raw file text with original line endings and no line-number prefixes; the covered line range is reported separately. Read a window, not a whole file: when a search hit already tells you where to look, send line with that line number to open a window around it, and raise radius only when the window proves too narrow. Send offset and limit instead to page through a file from a known point, continuing with the reported nextOffset. A call that sets neither returns the first lines of the file and reports its total length. Never list directories; use ls.
function.name: read

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Cannot be combined with line.

line.description: One-based line to centre a window on, such as the line a search hit reported. Cannot be combined with offset or limit.

offset.description: One-based line offset to begin reading. Cannot be combined with line.

path.description: One exact workspace-relative file path, copied character for character from a listing or search result. Not a directory, not a pattern, never a guessed name.

radius.description: Lines to show above and below line. Requires line.

function.description: List one workspace directory non-recursively. Entries are returned in lexical order with / on directories. Use find for recursion. Continue with nextOffset when truncated.
function.name: ls

path.description: One exact workspace-relative directory path, or "." for the workspace root. Not a file and not a pattern; ls has no glob argument.

function.description: Find workspace paths by one explicit glob under path. The two arguments split the shell form: the directory goes in path and the pattern goes in glob, so docs/*.md is {"path":"docs","glob":"*.md"}. Returns stable sorted relative paths. No fuzzy query language.
function.name: find

glob.description: One include glob, matched against both the workspace-relative path and the file name. Examples: **/*.rs, *.md, README*.

path.description: Existing workspace-relative directory to search under. Use "." for the workspace root. The pattern belongs in glob, never here.

function.description: Find workspace paths or text. This is the only text-search tool; do not shell out to ripgrep, grep, or find. path mode ranks files and directories by name. content mode matches exact literal text, and regex mode matches a regular expression; both return path:line: rows for each match, plus path:line- rows around them when context is set. Matching is case-insensitive unless query contains an uppercase character, which in regex mode an inline (?i) overrides. Set context to see the code around a match here instead of opening the file, and reserve read for what the surrounding lines do not settle. path is the directory scope and glob is the optional filename filter, so "find foo in internal/model/*.go" is {"query":"foo","mode":"content","path":"internal/model","glob":"*.go"}. Narrow path, glob, or query when a result is truncated.
function.name: search

context.description: Lines of surrounding code to show around each match. Ignored in path mode.

glob.description: Optional include glob such as *.md, matched against both the workspace-relative path and the file name.

limit.description: Maximum paths in path mode, or matches in content and regex mode. Defaults to 100 for path and 50 for the others.

mode.description: path ranks file and directory names; content and regex search inside files.

path.description: Existing workspace-relative file or directory to search under. Use "." for the workspace root. The filename pattern belongs in glob, never here.

query.description: Name fragment for path mode, exact literal text for content mode, or a regular expression for regex mode.

function.description: Search the public web. Returns titles, URLs, and short snippets. These are not full pages; call web_fetch with one result URL to read a page. An empty result is not proof the subject is missing from the web; never invent a domain. Send exactly query. Private and loopback hosts never appear.
function.name: web_search

query.description: The search query. Distill the question; do not paste the whole user prompt.

function.description: Read the text of one public web page. Use a URL from web_search or the user. Returns readable page text, not a screenshot or a browser. Private, loopback, link-local, and credentialed URLs are blocked. Send exactly url.
function.name: web_fetch

url.description: One absolute http or https URL.

function.description: Create or replace one workspace text file after permission. Send exactly path and content. Parents are created after approval; the write is staged and installed atomically.
function.name: write

function.description: Apply one or more exact replacements to one workspace file after permission. Send exactly path and edits[]. Each oldText must match the same original snapshot uniquely and without overlap. Copy oldText verbatim from the latest read result, including its line endings. No fuzzy matching.
function.name: edit

edits.description: Exact replacements to apply to one original snapshot.

function.description: Apply one exact Begin Patch document to workspace files after permission. Send exactly the patch field. Every hunk must match uniquely. Do not send edit fields.
function.name: apply_patch

patch.description: A complete *** Begin Patch through *** End Patch document.

function.description: Create, inspect, and edit PowerPoint, Word, Excel, and PDF files. Send a spec or a list of ops as JSON; never write library code and never open the file yourself. inspect requires path and returns origin, editSurface, unsupported[], and an outline whose ids the other two actions address. create requires format and spec. edit requires path and ops[]. Inspect any file you did not just create before editing it: editSurface says which ops are allowed, and ids you did not read from an outline do not exist. Results carry qa[]; fix every error and call again, at most three rounds. Nothing is written when ok is false.
function.name: artifact

action.description: inspect reads a file; create builds a new one from spec; edit applies ops to an existing one.

format.description: Required for create. Inferred from the extension of path for inspect and edit.

ops.description: Edit operations in order, each addressing ids reported by inspect. An op the file's editSurface does not allow is refused and nothing is written.

options.description: Optional switches such as {"tracked":true,"author":"Umbratic"} for a redlined Word edit.

out.description: Workspace-relative destination. Defaults to .umbratic/artifacts/<format>/<name>. On edit, omit it to write the result back over path.

path.description: Workspace-relative file to inspect or edit. Required for those two actions.

spec.description: The document specification for create, in this format's spec schema. Enums and content only: no coordinates, colours, or point sizes.

function.description: Run a local workspace command in /bin/sh after policy and permission checks. Prefer search to locate code and to show the lines around a match, read to open a window on a file, and ls or find for listing. Do not shell out to ripgrep, grep, or find for routine search. Optional timeoutMs has a bounded default and maximum. Output progress is coalesced; large output keeps the useful tail and remains retrievable by context hash. Send exactly command and optional timeoutMs. Do not send programId or args.
function.name: command

function.description: Run one approved executable by id without shell lookup. Send exactly programId, optional args, and optional timeoutMs. Put one argument value in each args item. Do not repeat the executable name, use shell operators, or send a command field.
function.name: run_program

args.description: Argument values only, in process order. Do not include the executable id.

programId.description: One exact executable id from this enum.

function.description: Retrieve a bounded window of exact compacted local tool output by its reported hash. Returns context_not_available when no output has been compacted yet.
function.name: retrieve_context

hash.description: The hash reported by a compacted tool result.
